newsitem.title: USA: Tyco offered $50/shr for American Standard.
newsitem.headline: Tyco offered $50/shr for American Standard.

text.p: Tyco International Ltd offered $50 per share for American Standard Cos Inc as part of a proposal to merge the two companies, according to a letter released by Tyco.

In the letter dated Dec 5 to American Standard chairman Emmanuel Kampouris, Tyco said a combination of the companies would benefit both and produce annual cost savings of a minimum of $150-200 million.
The letter was released by Tyco on Monday.
American Standard earlier Monday said it had rejected the offer and did not plan to hold discussions with Tyco.
Under the union proposed by Tyco, shareholders of American Standard would receive $50.00 per share of American Standard either in Tyco stock, cash, or a combination of both.
Tyco also proposed expanding the combined company's board of directors to 12, including the eight existing Tyco directors and four individuals from American Standard's board.

It said the principal offices of the combined companies would be located in the New York area and would not require the relocation of executive personnel. It also said the names of both companies would be incorporated in the new name of the combined company.
Tyco also said that JP Morgan had committed to lead financing arrangements required for the transaction as well as any refinancing needs.
Tyco said the proposed combination would be accretive to the earnings per share of Tyco.
In the letter signed by chief executive officer Dennis Kozlowski, Tyco invited American Standard to review its analysis and encouraged it to learn more about Tyco.
Tyco said it received a faxed rejection from American Standard the following day.
